title: TR3 from the second square: a commutative square on the second arrows extends to a morphism of distinguished triangles
statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{d}X[1]$ and $X'\xrightarrow{u'}Y'\xrightarrow{v'}Z'\xrightarrow{d'}X'[1]$ distinguished triangles, and $b:Y\to Y'$, $c:Z\to Z'$ morphisms with $c\circ v=v'\circ b$. Then there is $a:X\to X'$ with $b\circ u=u'\circ a$ and $a[1]\circ d=d'\circ c$, i.e. $(a,b,c)$ is a morphism of triangles.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, proof, p. 24 (pdf page 25): 'un argument dual fournit (a) <=> (b')' (the implication (b') => (c)); it is TR3 applied to the rotated triangles (TR2), literature/stacks-project/derived.tex Definition 0145 (definition-triangulated-category, line 95)
